root_idea.summary: The directly attested semantic center is black or fetid mud, especially as associated with wells and water.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence extends from the mud substance to conditions and actions involving it: water becoming turbid, wells being cleansed, and wells being filled with mud. Other homographic branches remain lexically distinct.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun for black or dark mud.
Quran-attested feminine adjective describing a spring fouled or darkened by mud.

senses.definition: Black or dark mud, including foul-smelling mud.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a noun for the mud substance named in the Quranic creation passage.

senses.definition: Foul or darkened by black, fetid mud.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine adjective describing a spring or well as fouled or darkened by such mud; in the Quranic occurrence it qualifies a spring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleanse a well of its black or fetid mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction with a well as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to become mixed with black, fetid mud, becoming turbid and altered in odor; of a well or spring, to contain such mud abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water, a well, or a spring.
The construction is used with عَلَيْهِ, ‘with’ or ‘against him’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw black or fetid mud into a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form IV construction with a well as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spouse’s male relation by marriage; especially a father-in-law, and in some usages a wife’s brother or paternal uncle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applies to the male relations of a woman’s husband or a man’s wife; the plural is أَحْمَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant growing in the sands and open or soft land of Najd.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regionally specified plant name, distinct from the mud term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An evil-eyed man whose gaze harms those whom he sees and admires.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed descriptive expression; no verb belonging to this expression is attested in the supplied evidence.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Water, well, and spring becoming or containing muddy water.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the mud entry.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the in-law entry.
Editorial pointer to the following entry.
A well or spring fouled with black, fetid mud.

cautions: The lexical record contains homographic or closely variant branches, including in-law terminology, a plant name, an evil-eye expression, and an anger verb; these are kept separate from the Quranic mud senses.
No Maqayis or Mufradat evidence was supplied, so root-level development beyond the directly attested lexical record is not asserted.
The well-cleaning construction is reported with a usage disagreement in the lexical evidence.
